identity: Arabic literary translation of the opening of A. S. Byatt, Ragnarok: The End of the Gods. Third-person past-tense narrative prose about a thin child in wartime England, her schoolteacher mother, her absent airman father, and the illustrated book Asgard and the Gods. It is a book-chapter layout, not an article: a title line, three heading lines (The Grey Ash Yggdrasil / The End of the World / 1 The Beginning) each isolated as its own one-line paragraph between <NL> tokens, ordinary long narrative paragraphs, and a run of four very short one-sentence paragraphs in the middle (1006-1015, 1017-1023, 1025-1030, 1032-1050) which the format itself hands me as calibrated, ground-truth sentence units of 6 to 19 tokens.
law: A sentence is one complete predication plus everything subordinated to it. This translator writes long, heavily coordinated periods, so a bare wa- plus verb that keeps the same subject (wa-tabaat 746, wa-rawadatha 598, wa-yaghlibu 443) and accusative wa-lists (the entire Riesengebirge catalogue 794-862, whose limbs wa-judhuan and wa-anasan are accusative objects of sawwarat) sit INSIDE a sentence and are never its edge. A boundary is licensed by one of three things. (a) ASYNDETON, a new finite predication with no connective at all: kana plus a new subject (54, 67, 249, 478, 527, 542), a bare perfect verb (584 qaraat, 794 sawwarat, 1117 hawalat, 1126 taallamu), kanat plus imperfect (418, 446, 731, 914), la budda (940), innaha (271), or an interrogative (623 man kana). (b) A SENTENCE-OPENING PARTICLE CLUSTER: amma...fa- (366, 717, 767), idhan (673), laqad (309), wa-maa dhalika (77, 560), wa-min thumma (120, 677), wa-qad plus perfect (225, 654, 760, 1108), wa-kana plus an explicit new subject (187, 234, 573, 1129). (c) A FRONTED ADVERBIAL that resets the scene (875 fi al-bidaya, 354 wa-fi nihayat kulli am, 128 wa-indama). Two discriminators do most of the work. First, contrastive wa-lakinna-HA carrying a resumptive clitic for the SAME subject stays inside the sentence (19, 304, 933, 1123), whereas wa-lakin followed by a fresh nominal subject opens a new one (315, 333). Second, fa- clauses are presumed bound to what precedes, and are cut only when the preceding unit is already a complete short assertion and the fa- clause is a long independent development. Structural givens: the token before every <NL> and the final token always close a sentence, an <NL> never carries one, and each heading line is a sentence.
reasoning: idx 36 (mararan | wa-hiya tiflatun nahilatun hazila). I read wa-hiya as opening a new nominal sentence, not as a hal. As a hal it would have to hang off her mother told her often, which is semantically empty; what follows is instead a 17-token standing description of the child (gaunt, bones like a newt, hair like fine mist), a fresh predication. The contrast that keeps me honest is idx 1036 wa-hiya tahduqu, a genuine hal with a verb, inside a 19-token paragraph that is demonstrably one sentence; that one I did not split. idx 119 and 127. I split twice. wa-min thumma nashaat fi al-jannati al-mahudati lil-rifi al-injlizi is a short resultative sentence in its own right, and wa-indama balaghat al-khamisa then opens the 40-token meadow sentence; joining all three would give one 88-token period, far outside anything else in this text. idx 193 (mufaraqat | fa-nazaran ila al-harb). LOW. The fa- binds tightly and a semicolon is as plausible as a period, but the preceding wa-kana masiru walidatiha aydan yantawi ala mufaraqat is a complete 7-token topic assertion and the fa- clause is a 31-token independent development, which is exactly my stated exception. Kept, weakly. idx 314 and 332. Two consecutive wa-lakin sentences, each carrying a fresh nominal subject (alamu al-rifi al-injlizi, then al-khawf), so both are cut. idx 345 (al-nahila | fa-hiya talamu bi-dakhiliha). NOT split: even if no one spoke of it to the thin child, FOR she knew inside herself that her father would not return, is a single causal period and the fa- is doing sentence-internal work. idx 403 (nafsuha | wa-lakinnaha fakkarat kathiran). NOT split, by the wa-lakinna-HA rule. She thought little, or so it now seems, about where she came from, but she thought a great deal about that old question, is one contrastive period; the same reasoning kills 18, 303 and 932. idx 594 (wa-ajaibihi | wa-hayyaratha fikratu al-alman). LOW. She read the introduction, which spoke of the recovery of the old Germanic world with its secrets and wonders, closes cleanly; the psych-verb pair hayyaratha and wa-rawadatha then runs on as one sentence, so I cut before the pair and not inside it (597 is not a boundary). idx 676 (qisasuha | wa-min thumma asbaha al-kitabu shaghafaha). LOW. Two very short closers of 4 and 5 tokens suit this author, and wa-min thumma behaves as a sentence opener at 120, but a single 9-token period is equally readable. idx 745 (al-yas | wa-tabaat asfarahu). NOT split. Bare wa- plus verb with the same subject is the paradigm case of coordination inside one sentence, and the Riesengebirge paragraph is my calibration for how far this translator will run a wa-chain: 69 tokens, one sentence. idx 772 (kadhalika | fa-hadha al-kitabu huwa qissatu lughz). LOW, the same exception as 193: a complete 6-token amma-sentence followed by a 20-token explanation. idx 788 and 790 (nihaya | nihaya haqiqiyya | nihayatu al-alam). LOW, and correlated, since either both are periods or neither is. Arabic would ordinarily coordinate or comma an apposition; the bare unlinked triple reads instead as staccato emphasis carried over from the source, and nihayatu al-alam is the leitmotif that is also the heading at 379-380. I take the periods while accepting that commas are nearly as likely. idx 862 (taqra | fa-wasalat al-qiraa). LOW. So she read on, as a 2-token closing sentence. This cuts against my own fa-binding presumption, but hanging between these shapes and the child AS SHE READ, so she continued reading, is redundant inside one period. idx 874 (al-asatir). Split before the asyndetic fi al-bidaya. But 887 (thumma asbahat) and 893 (wa-akhiran utubirat) are NOT split: this paragraph is the quoted Wagner passage, a single at-first / then / finally period, and thumma and wa-akhiran are its internal joints, not its edges. idx 1066 (al-muqaddas | wa-hunaka yuamiluhum al-qass). NOT split, though it is the closest call in the document. The wa- plus fronted locative explicitly ties the clause to the church just named, and 27 tokens is an unremarkable single period here. idx 1087 (al-tayyib | wa-zahara fi wahidatin minha). LOW, cut mainly on the tense shift from present tujad to perfect zahara, which is awkward inside one period. idx 1128 (al-salawat | wa-kana lada al-tiflati al-nahilati hads). Cut on the subject change from they learned to the child, with wa-kana plus an explicit new subject. Also rejected on coordination grounds: 483 (wa-ala ghilafihi sura, still inside the cover description), 272 (fa-huwa dhu sharin dhahabi), 597, 957. Density check: 69 boundaries over about 1140 non-<NL> tokens, roughly 16.5 tokens per sentence, which sits right on the length of the four short single-sentence paragraphs the format gives me for free.
